moments.title: The move south
moments.text: Chicago's first Chinese enclave had grown up in the late 1800s along Clark St between Van Buren and Harrison in the Loop. Facing rising rents, a planned federal building on those blocks, and prejudice, businesses tied to the On Leong Merchants Association moved south in 1912 to Wentworth Ave and 22nd St, now Cermak Rd.

moments.title: The On Leong building
moments.text: The On Leong Merchants Association's ornate headquarters opened on Wentworth Ave; some sources say it was built in 1927. It became a Chicago Landmark on Dec 1, 1993, and is now the Pui Tak Center.

moments.title: The Chinatown Gate
moments.text: A gate was built over Wentworth Ave near Cermak Rd as the neighborhood's formal entrance.

moments.title: Today: Chinatown
moments.text: Chinatown, centered on Wentworth Ave and Cermak Rd, is still home to Chicago's Chinese community, with its gate over Wentworth.
